# Performance report

The kernel runs 1.41x faster over the two configurations (geometric mean).

| config | baseline us | best us | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| n1024 | 812.4 | 590.1 | 1.38x |
| n2048 | 6400.0 | 4400.0 | 1.45x |

# Code modification report

`matmul.cu` stages 16 x 16 tiles of `a` and `b` in shared memory, so each global element is read once per tile.

# Optimization process report

The trace showed every thread waiting on global loads in the dot-product loop. Iteration 1 tiled the loads; iteration 2 unrolled the inner loop and was reverted.

# Hypothesis

Each thread reads a row of `a` and a column of `b` from global memory; tiling them in shared memory cuts the global reads by the tile width.
